messages.content: Write a polished short scene in modern American English between two adult friends talking about a minor personal problem while doing a simple household task. Let the physical task interrupt and shape the conversation naturally. Allow unfinished thoughts, interruptions, and topic shifts. Keep the characters grounded and avoid making the dialogue sound scripted or perfectly organized.

“I think I need to call him.”

Morgan was kneeling beside the cabinet, trying to get a pan unstuck from a stack of other pans.

“Maybe.”

“That's not helpful.”

“I wasn't trying to be helpful.”

Morgan pulled harder.

The bottom pan moved half an inch.

“There.”

“What?”

“The pan.”

Casey looked over. “Do you need a hand?”

“No.”

“You're making that face.”

“What face?”

“The one where you're about to declare war on cookware.”

Morgan laughed under her breath.

“I can get it.”

“Okay.”

She tried again.

Nothing.

“Maybe call him after dinner,” Casey said.

Morgan stopped pulling.

“Why?”

“Because you haven't eaten.”

“I had lunch.”

“When?”

Morgan thought about it.

“I don't know.”

“Exactly.”

She finally got the pan loose. It came free so suddenly that she nearly dropped it.

“Got it.”

Casey smiled. “Congratulations.”

Morgan stood and set the pan on the counter.

“You're avoiding my question.”

“No. I'm avoiding helping you make a decision when you're hungry.”

Morgan opened the refrigerator.

“There's leftover chicken.”

“Good.”

She pulled out the container.

“Then I'll eat first.”

Casey nodded.

“And then I'll call him.”

“Maybe.”

Morgan pointed the container at her.

“That's twice now.”

“I stand by it.”

Morgan smiled.

“Annoying.”

“Consistent.”

She put the chicken in the microwave.

Casey closed the cabinet door she'd left open.

Neither mentioned the phone again until the microwave beeped.
